reasons: No test was found for this data file.
Links to builds and research threads are checked only by hand.

terms.meaning: The one-line idea that sums up a curiosity.
A short name made of lowercase words and dashes, used as a stable id in addresses and links.
The visual motif, meaning the drawing style used for a curiosity's card.
A named line of inquiry that a curiosity feeds into.

sections.name: Curiosity
sections.title: Shape of a curiosity entry
sections.what: Defines what one curiosity holds: a title, a role, a year, a status, a plain text and a technical text, tags, a thesis line, the builds it produced, an optional research thread, and a visual motif for its card.
sections.why: Likely reason: one consistent shape lets the page and the brain show every curiosity the same way.
sections.watch_out: The visual motif accepts only six fixed names, so a new one needs matching drawing code elsewhere as well.

sections.name: curiosities (part 1)
sections.title: Industrial AI, strategy and portfolio curiosities
sections.what: Holds the first three curiosities: agentic AI for heavy industry, the AI strategy consulting platform, and the portfolio opportunity tracker. Each has a plain text, a technical text, tags and a thesis, and some link to a research thread and to the builds they produced.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The text is written in the first person, so it reads as the owner's own explanation rather than a neutral summary.
sections.watch_out: Build links use project slugs rather than build names, so a renamed slug quietly breaks the link to the build.

sections.name: curiosities (part 2)
sections.title: Careers, sport and compute curiosities
sections.what: Holds the rest of the curiosities: the careers idea behind Career OS, the AI for cricket idea, and an open thinking piece about hyper-personal computing, which is marked as ongoing and has no builds yet.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The compute entry is marked as ongoing and has no builds, so it reads as an idea rather than finished work.
sections.watch_out: Entries with an empty builds list, such as the compute idea, need the page to handle having nothing to show.

summary: Holds the owner's curiosities, which are longer-running interests and ideas, each with plain and technical text and the builds it produced.
purpose: Supplies the data for the curiosities section and for the right side of the brain picture.
why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond all curiosities sharing one shape.
how: First, the shape of a curiosity is defined. Then each curiosity is listed in order, with a title, role, year, status, plain and technical text, tags, a one-line thesis, linked builds, an optional research thread, and a visual style for its card.
inputs: Typed in by hand. The file reads no outside data.
outputs: An exported list of curiosities, read by the brain file and by the curiosities page, whose path is not visible in this packet.
risks: Linked builds and research threads are plain text and must match other files by hand. The thesis is typed separately from the text, so editing the text does not update it.
debug: If a curiosity has no links in the brain, check its builds values against project slugs and its thread id against the research threads. If a card looks wrong, check the plate name.
